Treasures in Heaven
TREZH-erz in HEV-en
noun phrase (Matthew 6:20)
From the Authorized Version of the Sermon on the Mount; the enduring riches the disciple is to lay up with God, against the perishing treasures of earth.

📖 Biblical Definition

Treasures in heaven are the enduring riches that the disciple of Christ is commanded to lay up with God, in contrast to the perishing treasures of earth. In the Sermon on the Mount the Lord commands, “Lay not up for yourselves treasures upon earth, where moth and rust doth corrupt, and where thieves break through and steal: but lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven… For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.” The teaching is not that wealth is sin, nor that the believer earns heaven by giving, but that he is to invest his life and substance in what cannot perish, securing for himself a treasure in the heavens that faileth not. These heavenly treasures include the eternal inheritance kept for the saints, the reward of grace for faithful service, and the fruit of generosity, of suffering for Christ, and of souls won. The Lord grounds the command in a law of the heart: a man's treasure draws his affections, so that he who heaps earthly riches binds his heart to a dying world, while he who lays up treasure in heaven sets his affection on things above. The dictionary holds the doctrine against two errors. The prosperity gospel inverts the Lord's words, promising earthly treasure as the reward of faith and binding the heart to the very mammon Christ warned against. The opposite error, a false asceticism, despises all earthly goods as evil rather than using them as stewardship toward heaven. The believer is to hold the things of earth loosely and lay up what endures, that his heart may be where his true and lasting riches are.

📜 Webster 1828 Definition

The enduring riches the disciple lays up with God (Matthew 6:20), against the perishing treasures of earth; for where the treasure is, the heart follows—the rebuke of the prosperity gospel and of mammon-bound affections alike.

TREASURES IN HEAVEN, noun phrase. The enduring riches the disciple lays up with God, beyond the reach of moth, rust, and thief.

“Lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven… For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also” (Matthew 6:20-21).

Against earthly treasures, where moth and rust corrupt and thieves steal (Matthew 6:19).

A treasure in the heavens that faileth not, where no thief approacheth (Luke 12:33).

Not earning heaven, but investing the life and substance in what cannot perish.

📖 Key Scripture

Mt 6:20 — "But lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust doth corrupt, and where thieves do not break through nor steal:"

Mt 6:21 — "For where your treasure is, there will your heart be also."

Mt 6:19 — "Lay not up for yourselves treasures upon earth, where moth and rust doth corrupt, and where thieves break through and steal:"

Lu 12:33 — "Sell that ye have, and give alms; provide yourselves bags which wax not old, a treasure in the heavens that faileth not, where no thief approacheth, neither moth corrupteth."

⚠️ Modern Corruption

The prosperity gospel inverts the Lord's words, promising earthly treasure as faith's reward, while a false asceticism despises earthly goods rather than stewarding them toward heaven.

expand to see more

The prosperity gospel directly contradicts the Lord's command, promising believers earthly treasure—wealth, health, prosperity—as the reward of faith and giving. This binds the heart to the very mammon Christ told His disciples not to lay up, and makes the gospel a means to the riches that moth and rust corrupt. The dictionary names it a corruption: the Lord commanded treasure laid up in heaven, not on earth, and warned that no man can serve God and mammon. The preacher who promises earthly gain in exchange for faith preaches the opposite of the Sermon on the Mount.

The opposite corruption is a false asceticism that treats all earthly goods as evil, despising property, comfort, and provision as though poverty were itself holiness. But the Lord does not forbid the use of earthly things; He forbids the hoarding of them as treasure and the binding of the heart to them. The believer is a steward who holds the goods of earth loosely and lays up what endures—by generosity, by faithful service, by suffering for Christ, by winning souls. The dictionary recovers the doctrine: earthly things are to be used for heavenly ends, and the heart set where the true treasure is, with God.

🔗 Greek & Hebrew Roots

From the Greek thesauros (a treasure, store, or treasury), whence “thesaurus”; the heavenly treasure is laid up (thesaurizo) where no corruption can reach it.

expand to see more

Thesauros, Greek, a treasure or storehouse, the word in Matthew 6:20.

Thesaurizo, Greek, to lay up or store treasure.

“Moth” (ses) and “rust” (brosis, eating away) figure the decay of earthly goods.

“Mammon” (Aramaic, riches personified) is the rival master Christ names.

“Where your treasure is” sets the law of the heart following its treasure.

Usage

"The pastor preached treasures in heaven to rebuke the prosperity gospel that binds the heart to earthly gain."

"He held his property loosely, laying up what endures by generosity and faithful service."

"She set her affection on things above, knowing her heart would follow her treasure."
